metadata.note: The Monon - the Chicago, Indianapolis and Louisville Railway and its predecessors the New Albany and Salem and the Louisville, New Albany and Chicago - drawn from a research report written in the companion site repo (research/branches/chicago_indianapolis_and_louisville_railway.txt, 2026-08-30) and converted on 2026-09-30. Before this layer the map drew no Monon route at all. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn, which keep to years a source confirms; several end decades before the rails came up. The railroad's two through routes cross at Monon, Indiana: Chicago - Lafayette - Bloomington - Louisville and Michigan City - Monon - Delphi - Indianapolis. The 1859, 1897 and 1956 name changes are one railroad and share one colour; Rule 4 splits are drawn only where another company ran the trains (Indianapolis, Delphi and Chicago to 1881, Bedford and Bloomfield to 1886, Chicago and Wabash Valley to 1914). The Monon merged into the Louisville and Nashville on 31 July 1971, after its last passenger train, so there is no L&N-coloured successor feature.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS - these end years are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: Michigan City - Monon stops at 1914 (passengers certainly gone by 1951, end year unknown); Bedford - Switz City stops at 1895 (ended before the 1935 abandonment, year unknown); McCoysburg - Zadoc stops at 1929. Start-year conflict: Delphi - Indianapolis is drawn from 1884 (first Fowler letter) though the Air Line reached Indianapolis in 1882 and secondary sources say passenger service began in 1883. French Lick branch mileage conflicts: 17.7 mi (Fowler, american-rails) vs 18.88 mi (abandonedonline). Relocation dates are unknown for the Clear Creek - Smithville - Harrodsburg line and the Lafayette Fifth Street line (Fowler: "until 1970's?"), so both are drawn on their later alignments. All headways and speeds are estimates. Station-level data (Rule 8) has not been started for this railroad.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: Victoria Branch (Wallace Junction - Victoria): Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 3 is headed "Freight Service only" and no passenger year is confirmed; Fowler's undated "served by miners trains" is not enough to draw. Its mine spurs are freight. Chicago - Maynard (1882-1885, over C&WI and PRR track, terminal uncertain). New Albany - Louisville over the PRR Jeffersonville bridge (1870s-1886, entirely PRR track). Zadoc - Kersey (confirmed 1905 only) and Kersey - Dinwiddie (Fowler marks every station "pass?"). The original Cedar Lake and Smithville alignments as separate features (no relocation date for Smithville; the Cedar Lake grade is mostly unmapped). The Red Devil (Indianapolis - French Lick, joint with the PRR): routing not sourced; where it used Monon rail it is already drawn.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Victoria Branch (Feb 1952 Guide, Table 3, "Freight Service only"; index daggers on Victoria, Midland and Patricksburg). Michigan City line after its last confirmed year, French Lick branch after September 1949 (the 1951-52 Guide entry is a motor bus), Switz City branch after 1895: in each case the drawn span stops at the last confirmed passenger year, not at abandonment.

APPROXIMATED: Dearborn Station - 18th Street (1.6 mi) is two straight lines, because the Chicago and Western Indiana throat south of Polk Street lies under Dearborn Park and is not mapped. 18th Street - Hammond (20.0 mi) is a shortest path, 12 mi of it on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator=C&WI and the rest on Metra Southwest Service, Indiana Harbor Belt and other terminal track; the actual C&WI routing the Monon used south of 74th Street is NOT sourced. Hammond - Monon (67.9 mi against 67.7 between Fowler's Hammond MP 20.7 and Monon MP 88.4) is entirely on the CSX Monon Subdivision with no straight-line bridges; every station town lies within 0.8 km of the line; the two traces meet with a 493 m gap at Hammond. LATER ALIGNMENT: passenger trains used an earlier line through Armour, Paisley and Creston at Cedar Lake (MP 38.4-44.8, 6.4 mi) until 1948 (Fowler line 1 note 2); this feature draws the post-1948 line for all years. OSM keeps only a 1.9 km fragment of the old grade, which runs up to about 600 m from the drawn line. The 1882-1885 approach over the C&WI and PRR via Maynard is not drawn (see metadata).

segments.note: The Louisville, New Albany and Chicago was reorganised as the Chicago, Indianapolis and Louisville Railway on 1 July 1897 and renamed the Monon Railroad on 11 January 1956 - one railroad under three names, drawn in one colour. In its last decades this carried the Thoroughbred (Chicago-Louisville, from 15 Feb 1948), the Hoosier and the Tippecanoe (Chicago-Indianapolis, streamlined 1947), the Night Express / Bluegrass (Chicago-Louisville, to September 1949) and briefly the Varsity (Chicago-Bloomington, 1950 and spring 1953); the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 1) shows Chicago departures with legible times. properties.geometry_quality: Traced: 230.7 mi Monon - New Albany against 229.2 mi between Fowler's mileposts (Monon MP 88.4, New Albany MP 317.6). 173 mi is on OSM ways tagged as the Monon (the live CSX Monon Subdivision north of Bloomington, Indiana Rail Road and lifted Hoosier Subdivision grade south of it). 53 mi comes from OpenHistoricalMap where OSM maps nothing: Cloverdale - Gosport - Ellettsville (27 mi, the lifted line through Owen and Monroe counties), Bloomington - Harrodsburg (10 mi), and Salem - Borden (10 mi), with short OHM pieces at Bedford, Mitchell and Orleans. LATER ALIGNMENTS, all drawn back to 1854: (1) Lafayette: from 1854 through 1967 trains ran down Fifth Street (Fowler line 1 note 3, Lafayette Shops MP 118.2 - Lafayette Junction MP 121.5); this draws the relocated line along the river, roughly 300-400 m west of Fifth Street for about 3 mi. (2) Clear Creek - Harrodsburg (about 9 mi): the original line ran via Smithville and Sanders (confirmed in passenger use 1875 and 1914, relocation date unknown); this draws the later line through Harrodsburg, up to 4.3 km from Smithville. OpenHistoricalMap has the Smithville line, but with no date for the change the feature cannot be split honestly. (3) Street running in Bedford and New Albany is not reconstructed.

The Monon took charge on 15 March 1914 after Gifford's death; the later years are a separate Monon feature. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
